services.title: What Aura Historia does.
services.description: Four services with one aim: to help you find the right object, and keep it in view until you decide.

search.title: One search across the market
search.description: Dealers, auction houses, specialist shops and marketplaces in one search. Listings are translated and their terms aligned, so a query in your language also finds objects catalogued in another. You see what is offered now, then open the original listing to buy or bid.

watchlist.title: Private watchlist

story.origin: Aura Historia began in Leipzig in 2026. It grew out of a collector’s experience that the objects worth finding surface far from the obvious channels: with specialist dealers, smaller shops, auction houses and marketplaces, each with its own language and cataloguing habits.
story.today: We set out to bring order to that search without turning it into a generic shopping experience. Today a team of five builds Aura Historia, across web engineering, data automation, interface design and knowledge graph engineering.

lucaFranke.bio: Luca leads the web application work, translating Aura Historia’s research and discovery goals into a reliable, maintainable product experience. Luca previously worked on web and app development for marketplaces.

abdellahFilali.bio: Abdellah works on the automation behind source ingestion, data quality, and repeatable processes that help the platform follow a fragmented market at scale. Abdellah previously worked on automated data extraction for job platforms.

erwinBause.bio: Erwin shapes the interface and interaction details so Aura Historia remains calm, legible, and respectful of how collectors and specialists actually research objects. Erwin previously worked on UI/UX design for consumer applications.

antonDiettrich.bio: Anton works on the knowledge graph foundations that connect objects, sources, categories, and market context with more structure and continuity. Anton previously worked on knowledge graph engineering and on question answering built on knowledge graphs.

whatIs.question: What is Aura Historia?
whatIs.answer: Aura Historia is a global search engine for art and antiques, based in Leipzig, Germany. It brings listings from dealers, auction houses and marketplaces into one multilingual search, with private watchlists and search alerts.

whoIsBehind.question: Who is behind Aura Historia?
whoIsBehind.answer: Aura Historia is built by a team of five, across web engineering, data automation, interface design and knowledge graph engineering. It is based in Leipzig, Germany.

isFree.question: Is Aura Historia free?
isFree.answer: Yes. Searching needs no account, and a free account adds a private watchlist of 20 objects and one search alert. Collectors who follow many objects at once can choose a paid plan with more room for both.

buyDirectly.question: Can I buy through Aura Historia?
buyDirectly.answer: No. Purchases take place with the original seller: we link to the source listing, where you confirm price, condition, shipping and payment before you buy or bid.

appraisal.question: Does Aura Historia appraise or authenticate objects?
appraisal.answer: No. Listings are shown as their sources publish them, translated where needed. Questions of value, condition and authenticity are settled with the seller.

barnebys.question: How is Aura Historia different from Barnebys?
barnebys.answer: Barnebys is strongest around auction houses. Aura Historia also indexes dealers, specialist shops and marketplaces, aligns listings across five languages and checks for changes continuously. Our comparison page sets out the differences in detail.

faq.title: Asked, and answered.

howItWorks.question: What is Aura Historia?
howItWorks.answer: Aura Historia is a global platform for art, antiques and distinctive objects. We bring current inventory from dealer sites, auction houses, marketplaces, and specialist sources into one place so collectors and professionals can follow the market with clarity.

directPurchase.question: Can I buy directly through Aura Historia?
directPurchase.answer: Purchases take place with the original seller. Aura Historia takes you to the source listing so you can verify price, availability, shipping, condition, and payment terms directly before you buy or bid.

priceAlerts.question: What can I monitor?
priceAlerts.answer: Your private watchlist keeps found objects in view and can notify you about relevant changes such as price movements or status updates. Search alerts monitor the market for new matches that fit your criteria.

language.question: Does Aura Historia work across languages?
language.answer: Yes. Aura Historia is built for international discovery: listings may appear in different languages, categories, and dealer vocabularies. The platform helps bridge that fragmentation without requiring you to know every local term.

updateFrequency.question: How current are the listings?
updateFrequency.answer: We refresh sources continuously. Final availability, however, always belongs to the dealer, auction house, or marketplace, so critical details should be checked on the original listing before purchase or bid.

dealers.question: Which sources are included?
dealers.answer: We include trusted dealers, specialist shops, auction houses, and marketplaces — including smaller sources that are often less visible on auction-focused platforms. Coverage is expanded continuously.

dealerRequest.question: Can I suggest a dealer or source?
dealerRequest.answer: Yes. Send the URL and a short note to contact@aura-historia.com. We review whether the source is relevant, reputable, and technically suitable for inclusion.

comparisonBarnebys.question: How is Aura Historia different from auction aggregators?
comparisonBarnebys.answer: Auction aggregators are strongest around upcoming or past auction lots. Aura Historia looks at the market more broadly: dealer inventory, specialist shops, marketplaces, and auctions in one platform — with watchlists, search alerts, and market monitoring.

comparisonPriceDatabase.question: Is Aura Historia a price database?
comparisonPriceDatabase.answer: No. Historical auction prices can be useful, but they do not automatically show what is available now. Aura Historia focuses on current discovery, monitoring, and timely market signals.

asyncAdmission.title: Admission outcomes
asyncAdmission.description: POST, PATCH, PUT and DELETE on /product-listings/async take the same entries, maxItems 100. HTTP 202 means at least one entry was confirmed admitted, or the batch was empty; admitted entries are then processed for you, with nothing to poll. The report is { submissionId, acceptedCount, failures }: acceptedCount plus failures equals the entries sent, and each failure has index, error, retryable and, when safe to echo, sourceListingId. With nothing admitted: 503 for unconfirmed, retryable or blocked sends; otherwise 500 for internal failures; 413 when only size failed; otherwise 400. Listing existence, auctions and provider authority are checked during processing.

asyncIdempotency.title: Idempotency and retries
asyncIdempotency.description: Send one Idempotency-Key header: 1–128 visible ASCII characters, no comma. Without one, a key is generated and echoed on the report; if that response is lost, the key cannot be recovered. After a lost or uncertain response, resend the exact batch, unchanged and in the same order, with the same key, rejected entries included. retryable marks failures where that resend is appropriate (ENQUEUE_UNCONFIRMED may already be queued); validation and size errors are not retryable. Correct invalid entries in a new request with a new key, leaving out admitted and uncertain ones. submissionId is for correlation only. To look at listings yourself, use GET on /product-listings; delegated tokens also need product-listings:read.

syncOutcomes.description: POST, PATCH, PUT and DELETE on /product-listings: maxItems 100; [] returns HTTP 200 with []. Each entry runs in its own transaction. On partial success, HTTP 200 returns only failures as { listingSourceId, sourceListingId, error }. If every non-empty entry fails, the first failure becomes an application/problem+json response. Do not replay successful entries.
syncOutcomes.title: Completed-write outcomes

create.title: Create fields and prices
create.description: POST requires sourceListingId, url and images; include localized title and description when available (the current contract allows omission or null). Seller and address fields are not supported. Availability is nullable. Asking price is { type: MONETARY, currency: EUR, amount: 420000 } in minor currency units, or { type: ON_REQUEST }; null records no price.

patch.title: Preserve or clear
patch.description: Omitted members preserve existing facts. null clears title, description, availability, price and each price estimate. url: null, images: null and auction: null are invalid (400 BAD_BODY_VALUE). images: [] clears images. The complete batch contract is validated before entry transactions begin.

put.title: Upsert semantics
put.description: For existing listings, omit title, description, availability or prices to preserve, send null to clear or a value to set. Omit images to preserve, [] to clear, or an array to replace; null is invalid. Omit url or send null to preserve; a URL replaces it. New listings require sourceListingId, url and images; omitted/null title, description, availability and prices record no value.

auction.title: Auction membership and lot timing
auction.description: Omit auction to preserve its context; auction: null is invalid. Within auction, auctionId must identify an existing auction for the same provider: omit to preserve membership, null to clear, an ID to set. For lotNumber, cataloguePosition and each timing leaf (biddingOpens, scheduledCloses, reportedClosedAt), omit to preserve, null to clear, or supply a value to set. Timing values are RFC3339 instants.

withdrawal.title: Batch withdrawal and restoration
withdrawal.description: DELETE takes an array of { sourceListingId } on either path. It withdraws listings, which is reversible, and preserves their history; PUT restores a withdrawn listing before applying current facts. Read the outcome by your mode: the admission report for asynchronous, failed entries for synchronous.

async.label: Asynchronous
async.title: Admitted now, processed for you.
async.response: HTTP 202 returns an admission report: submissionId, acceptedCount and one failure for each entry not confirmed admitted.
async.failures: Admitted entries go ahead. Listing existence, auctions and provider authority are checked during processing, not in the response. With nothing admitted, 400, 413, 500 or 503 returns the same report.
async.retry: After a lost or uncertain response, resend the unchanged batch with the same Idempotency-Key. Fix invalid entries in a new batch with a new key.
async.afterwards: Nothing to poll: once admitted, an entry is in our hands and processed for you. To look anyway, read listings back with GET; delegated tokens also need product-listings:read.

sync.label: Synchronous
sync.title: Completed writes, in the response.
sync.response: HTTP 200 lists failed entries only; [] means every entry completed, an empty batch included.
sync.failures: Each entry has its own transaction, so completed writes stay committed. If every entry fails, a problem response is returned instead.
sync.retry: Correct and resend only the failed entries.
sync.afterwards: Search visibility follows separately; a completed write is not yet visible in search.

Aura Historia starts from a wider premise: collectors should be able to search art, antiques and design objects across dealers, auction houses and marketplaces in one place.

summary.title: The short version
summary.paragraph1: Aura Historia is a broader alternative to Artsy for collectors who want antiques and design objects alongside art, and who want to see dealers, auction houses and marketplaces rather than one platform's partners.
summary.paragraph2: Artsy remains the natural place to follow contemporary artists through their galleries, with editorial and artist context around the works. Aura Historia searches across providers and languages, and lets you watch across providers rather than within a single inventory.

respect.title: Artsy brought gallery art to a wide audience
respect.paragraph1: A fair comparison starts here: Artsy brought gallery inventory, artist information and editorial to a wide audience. According to its own website (November 2026), it offers more than 1 million artworks from thousands of galleries and auction houses, and more than 3.4 million collectors and enthusiasts use it.
respect.paragraph2: Artist profiles, exhibitions, fairs and editorial put the works in context. Aura Historia does not try to replace that. It answers a different question: what is on offer across dealers, auction houses and marketplaces.
respect.status: On 15 April 2026, Artsy and Artnet announced that they had joined forces under shared leadership. According to the announcement, both will continue to operate as distinct brands and websites.

advantages.title: Antiques and design, different kinds of providers, one place to watch
advantages.description: The difference is scope: antiques and design objects alongside art, many kinds of providers, and one search across them.

faq.title: Common questions about Aura Historia and Artsy

alternative.question: Is Aura Historia an Artsy alternative?
alternative.answer: Yes, for buyers who want to search beyond gallery listings. Aura Historia searches art, antiques and design objects across dealers, auction houses and marketplaces in one place. Artsy remains a well-known destination for gallery-represented contemporary art.

replace.question: Does Aura Historia replace Artsy?
replace.answer: Not for everyone. Artsy suits collectors who want to follow contemporary artists through their galleries. Aura Historia is the broader choice for art, antiques and design objects from many kinds of providers, and the two can be used side by side.

antiquesAndDesign.question: Which service is better for antiques and design objects?
antiquesAndDesign.answer: Aura Historia. Antiques and design objects are part of what it searches, across dealers and auction houses. Artsy lists design as one of its mediums and has a Furniture and Design collection; it describes its offer in terms of contemporary and modern art.

galleryArt.question: Which service is better for contemporary art from galleries?
galleryArt.answer: Artsy. It is built around its partner galleries, which present their inventory, artists and shows on the platform, with editorial around them. Aura Historia shows listings from providers and does not represent galleries or artists.

summary.title: The short version
summary.paragraph1: Aura Historia is the better Barnebys alternative for collectors, dealers, researchers, and anyone who needs broad art and antiques discovery rather than auction aggregation alone.
summary.paragraph2: Barnebys deserves credit for its history in auction search. Aura Historia wins the practical comparison by indexing more source types, translating and normalizing listing text, monitoring changes near real-time, and building on modern AI-assisted search.

respect.title: Barnebys helped define auction aggregation
respect.paragraph1: A fair comparison should start here: Barnebys is a known name in the art and antiques auction world. For many buyers, it made scattered auction-house catalogues feel more searchable and approachable.
respect.paragraph2: That is useful. It is also not the same as seeing the whole online market. The objects collectors want are spread across major auction houses, regional auctioneers, specialist dealers, independent shops, marketplaces, and sometimes private sellers. Aura Historia is designed for that wider reality.
respect.status: Barnebys Group AB was declared bankrupt by the Stockholm District Court on 11 March 2026, on its own application. According to Barnebys' privacy policy (updated 3 August 2026), Boje Group AB has acquired the business and continues to operate the Barnebys service.

advantages.title: More sources, near real-time signals, fewer language barriers

marketBeyondAuctions.title: The market beyond auction catalogues

nearRealTimeAlerts.title: Near real-time alerts

languagePenalties.title: Search without language penalties

aiForwardMatching.title: AI-forward matching

Databases such as the Artnet Price Database, WorthPoint, MutualArt and Artprice record what objects sold for. respect.title: Price databases give access to auction results

WorthPoint's results announcement of January 2022 cited more than 610 million archived prices. MutualArt says it has data on more than 900,000 artists (November 2026).
respect.paragraph2: These are the companies' own figures. They count different things, so this page does not add them up or compare them with any figure of Aura Historia. Price research is their work. Aura Historia answers a different question: what is offered now, by whom, and what has changed since. It gives no valuations.
respect.status: On 15 April 2026, Artsy and Artnet announced that they had joined forces under shared leadership. According to the announcement, both will continue to operate as distinct brands and websites. The announcement still lists the Artnet Price Database among Artnet's services.

faq.title: Common questions about Aura Historia and price databases

alternativeArtnet.question: Is Aura Historia an Artnet alternative?
alternativeArtnet.answer: Not in the usual sense. The Artnet Price Database records what objects sold for: Artnet describes it as about 18 million auction results, with records back to 1985 (its Price Database page, November 2026). Aura Historia shows what dealers, auction houses and marketplaces offer now. The two answer different questions and work well together. Aura Historia gives no valuations.

alternativeWorthPoint.question: Is Aura Historia a WorthPoint alternative?
alternativeWorthPoint.answer: Not in the usual sense. WorthPoint is a price database: its results announcement of January 2022 cited more than 610 million archived prices, collected from online marketplaces and auction houses. Aura Historia shows what dealers, auction houses and marketplaces offer now. Use WorthPoint to research past prices and Aura Historia to see current offers. Aura Historia gives no valuations.

alternativeArtpriceMutualArt.question: Is Aura Historia an Artprice or MutualArt alternative?
alternativeArtpriceMutualArt.answer: Not in the usual sense. Artprice and MutualArt both give access to auction results: Artprice's parent company says its databanks hold over 30 million indices and auction results (November 2026), and MutualArt says it has data on more than 900,000 artists (November 2026). Aura Historia shows what dealers, auction houses and marketplaces offer now. MutualArt also describes online appraisals, which Aura Historia does not offer.

worth.question: Can Aura Historia tell me what my object is worth?
worth.answer: No. Aura Historia gives no valuations or appraisals. It shows listings as the providers publish them, and an asking price is the provider's own. To find out what an object is worth, ask an appraiser, and use a price database to see what comparable objects have sold for.

similarOffers.question: Where can I see what similar objects are offered for?
similarOffers.answer: Search for the type of object. Results show dealers, auction houses, shops and marketplaces side by side, with their prices as published, so you can see where comparable objects are offered. A listing page adds that listing's own price history since Aura Historia first recorded it. Neither is a valuation, and past sale prices are the work of a price database.

pastResults.question: Does Aura Historia show past auction results?
pastResults.answer: Not as a results database. Aura Historia lists what providers offer and records changes to each listing from the day it first sees it, so a listing page shows its own price and availability history. A listing that sold or was withdrawn can stay visible, and where a sale has been observed the price is labelled “Observed sale price”. It is not an archive of auction results, and its history starts when Aura Historia first records a listing. For past results, use a price database.

consequences.correct: Correction keeps this location's identity. Listing sources that use it as their default keep it, and their inherited listing geography follows the corrected details after a short delay.
consequences.relocate: Relocation creates a new location with its own identity and retires this one in the same step. Listing sources that use this location as their default are not moved: they keep the retired reference and supply no inherited listing geography until a default is chosen explicitly.
consequences.retire: The location leaves public results and no longer supplies inherited listing geography; this can take a short time. Listing sources that use it as their default keep the reference for traceability, and no other location is selected automatically.
consequences.restore: The location becomes public again: its exact point, country and region can appear in search results. Listing sources that still reference it as their default supply inherited listing geography again after a short delay.

account.title: Signed in on your terms.
account.description: You approve once on our own page, see who is asking, and can end the connection whenever you like.

signIn.title: What sign-in asks for
signIn.body: One approval, the first time, to read and change four parts of your account. Our page shows the assistant’s name and the website it comes from, so you know who is asking.

duration.title: How long it lasts
duration.body: You stay signed in while you use it. After 30 days without use, and after 90 days in any case, your assistant asks you to sign in again.

disconnect.title: How to disconnect
disconnect.body: Choose Disconnect under Connected apps in your account. That assistant loses access at once, wherever you use it. To use it again, connect it and sign in once more.

account.privacy: Your assistant’s provider processes the results it receives under its own privacy policy. How we handle connections and sign-ins is set out in our <privacyLink>privacy policy</privacyLink>.

closing.title: We help you find it. You buy from the seller.
closing.body: Aura Historia is a discovery service. To buy or bid, you continue to the dealer’s or auction house’s own website, as you would from our search.
